original_question: For exponential families, are there systematic studies of cases where the space of expectation parameters is non-convex, and if not, can such a theory be developed?
target_in_paper: Section 7 (Tomonari SEI): the open problem beginning, 'Efron found an example of an exponential family in which the space of expectation parameters is not convex. Are there systematic studies on this phenomenon? If not, can we develop?' and sharpened at the end of the section to 'How to characterize possible shapes of non-convex expectation parameter spaces?'
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the right topic (exponential families), the right pathology (non-convex expectation-parameter space), and the paper’s exploratory tone about whether a systematic theory already exists or should be developed.
missing_details: The paper’s exact object is the expectation parameter space η(Θ), not an informal 'space of expectation parameters.'
Section 7 defines η(Θ) by η(Θ) = ∇ψ(Θ), where ψ is the potential (log-partition) function and Θ is the natural parameter domain.

The nearby context ties the phenomenon specifically to the non-steep case: by the cited Theorem 9.2 of Barndorff-Nielsen, ψ is steep if and only if η(Θ) coincides with the interior of the convex closure of the support.
Because of that theorem, the paper notes that non-convex expectation-parameter spaces can appear only when ψ is non-steep; this restriction is missing from the draft.
Section 7 further notes that, in such non-convex cases, the support of the underlying carrier measure must be unbounded; this hidden assumption is omitted in the draft.
The paper sharpens the broad 'can such a theory be developed?' wording into the more precise goal of characterizing the possible shapes of non-convex expectation parameter spaces.
The paper also records an example where η(Θ) is bounded but non-convex, so the refined question should not accidentally build in 'unbounded expectation-parameter space' as part of the problem.
To stay paper-faithful, the question should remain in Section 7’s setting of ordinary exponential families and not drift to the generalized exponential families discussed separately in Section 8.
The natural ambient parameter spaces are real Euclidean spaces (natural parameters in Θ and expectation parameters in η(Θ)); this is implicit in the paper but not stated in the draft.
refined_question: Let {P_θ}_{θ∈Θ} be an exponential family with natural parameter domain Θ ⊂ R^d, potential function ψ, and expectation parameter space η(Θ) := ∇ψ(Θ). Since Section 7 notes, via the cited Theorem 9.2 of Barndorff-Nielsen, that steepness forces η(Θ) to be the interior of the convex closure of the support, can one develop a systematic theory for the non-steep case that characterizes the possible shapes of non-convex expectation parameter spaces η(Θ), including the bounded non-convex examples exhibited there?
justification: This draft is aimed at Section 7, not at any other part of the paper. The opening sentence of Section 7 is already very close to your wording, and the same section immediately adds the notation η(Θ) = ∇ψ(Θ), the steepness criterion imported from Theorem 9.2 of the cited reference, the consequence that non-convexity can occur only in the non-steep setting with unbounded support, and finally the sharper formulation asking for a characterization of the possible shapes of non-convex expectation parameter spaces. The refined question therefore keeps your topic but makes it stand-alone, adds the paper’s hidden assumptions and notation, and narrows the scope to the exact Section 7 intent rather than broadening to neighboring themes such as generalized exponential families.

Definition of η(Θ) = ∇ψ(Θ) and the steepness criterion via Theorem 9.2 of the cited reference
Remark that non-convexity occurs only in the non-steep case and that the support must be unbounded
Example of bounded non-convex η(Θ), Figure 1, and concluding formulation asking to characterize possible shapes
